subject: Quantifying tail latency for CedarPoint integration — next steps
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@cedarpoint.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: CedarPoint Labs Infra <infra@cedarpoint.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call notes: tail/p95 targets and next asks

Hi Rachel / Ben — great call earlier. Quick recap and what we need from Redwood to move forward with a POC: 

Summary of our current observed metrics (production, mixed web + mobile traffic):
- p95 end-to-end (client->provider->client) for 1.2KB prompt payloads: ~420 ms
- p99 end-to-end for same workload: ~980 ms
- Typical sustained concurrency: ~120 active inference sessions; daily spikes up to ~700 concurrent sessions for 10-15 minutes
- Streaming behavior: clients use streaming partial tokens; we rely on first-chunk latency ~60% of perceived latency

What we want from Redwood:
1) A proposed test plan that compares Redwood hosted API -> our incumbent provider using identical replay traffic (we can provide request logs).
2) Instrumentation spec: we need p95/p99 E2E (client-observed), server-side processing, network RTT, and chunk-first-byte latency for streaming.
3) A suggested target SLO envelope for initial acceptance (we are open to Redwood recommendations).

Attaching our SLO requirements PDF (cpl_slo_requirements.pdf) and a short note with the traffic profile. Can you share a proposed test window and the minimal data we should provide?

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform, CedarPoint Labs
samir.gupta@cedarpoint.ai

---
Attachment: cpl_slo_requirements.pdf (application/pdf, 320 KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@cedarpoint.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call notes: tail/p95 targets and next asks

Samir — thanks for the clear recap and the SLO PDF. We can run the comparative POC and will instrument the same metrics you outlined. Quick proposed approach and asks: 

Proposed acceptance envelope (initial recommendation):
- p95 end-to-end: <= 200 ms for 1.2KB payloads
- p99 end-to-end: <= 600 ms
- First-chunk streaming latency: <= 120 ms

What we need from CedarPoint to schedule the run:
- A representative request replay (anonymized) covering 30 minutes of peak traffic and 2 hours of typical traffic.
- List of regions (we plan US-west + US-east runs) and any IP allowlists for test clients.
- Any mobile-proxy behavior you want included (you mentioned some mobile clients add tail variance).

Proposed test window: we can support Apr 20, 01:00–03:00 UTC (low production impact). Ben/marissa — can you confirm test harness availability and whether we should simulate 4x peak concurrency spikes?

I’ll hand this over to Ben/Marissa to draft the test plan CSV and schedule. We’ll mirror measurements against your current provider and surface delta charts and traces.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: test harness outline for CedarPoint POC

Marissa/Jonas — internal planning notes for the POC config (draft):

Test harness config (summary):
- Replay dataset: 30-min peak capture + 2-hr baseline from CedarPoint (we will replay from a dedicated test runner).
- Concurrency pattern: steady 120 RPS baseline, 10-minute spike to 700 concurrent sessions (repeat 3x). Include ramp up/down windows of 60s.
- Payload distributions: median 850 bytes, 95th 1.2 KB, 99th 2.8 KB.
- Streaming: enable chunked response mode; measure first-chunk latency (time to first byte of chunk) and total stream completion time.
- Cache warmup: seed KV cache with repeated prefixes for 15 minutes prior to measurement window.

Metrics to capture (high granularity):
- Client-observed E2E latency (millis) per request
- Server processing time (inference service)
- Network RTT (via synthetic probes)
- Per-chunk first-byte latency and inter-chunk spacing
- Resource utilization (GPU p99 latency on forward pass, queue depth)

Data outputs: delta table (Redwood vs incumbent) for p50/p95/p99, CDF plots, and per-request trace IDs for sample failure analysis.

Risks/notes:
- Mobile clients sometimes add 100–200 ms tail; include a mobile-proxy run.
- If streaming starts to bottleneck at high concurrency, we may need to test reduced chunk sizes (250–400 token chunks).

Assigning: Marissa to assemble CSV and schedule infra; Jonas to prepare trace/metric dashboards we will hand to CedarPoint. Rachel — please confirm the proposed window with Samir and secure any allowlists.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks, this looks good. Quick confirmations: 

- We will provide anonymized replay logs (S3 link) by EOD Apr 18.
- Allowlist: test runner IPs will be 34.210.45.12 and 52.44.33.98 (please confirm when you see traffic).
- Mobile caveat: our mobile clients (in certain regions) add an extra ~150 ms median network tail; please include a mobile-proxied run as you outlined.

Acceptance note: if Redwood can demonstrate >= 30% improvement in p99 over our incumbent while maintaining functional parity (no increased error rate / truncated streaming), we have internal approval to move to a month-long pilot.

I’ll share the S3 link and a short JSON with the replay manifest shortly. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Samir Gupta
